s1.syndrome_frame: Acute respiratory distress with facial and nasal swelling in a patient with recent COVID-19 infection and uncontrolled diabetes
salient_findings: Black eschar on the nasal root
Presence of fungal hyphae and spores in nasal mucosa
key_facts: Patient is a 67-year-old male
Patient has uncontrolled diabetes
Patient had COVID-19 infection at the end of December 2022
Patient was admitted to hospital on January 1st, 2023
Patient developed new symptoms on January 11th, including nasal ache, dyspnea, and facial and nasal swelling
Initial examination showed temperature of 36.5°C, heart rate of 116, respiratory rate of 26, blood pressure of 150/88 mmHg, and O2 saturation of 90% in room air
Laboratory tests showed white blood cell count of 2 × 10^9/L, creatinine of 178 umol/L, blood sugar of 11.6 mmol/L, and platelet count of 17 × 10^9/L
Imaging studies showed pansinusitis, bilateral lung infiltrations, and presence of fungal hyphae and spores in nasal mucosa
Blood metagenomics next-generation sequencing (mNGS) detected Rhizopus microsporum and Mucor racemosus

shortlist.label: Mucormycosis
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of fungal hyphae and spores in nasal mucosa, detection of Rhizopus microsporum and Mucor racemosus in blood mNGS, and clinical presentation of facial and nasal swelling

shortlist.label: Rhizopus infection
shortlist.why_kept: Detection of Rhizopus microsporum in blood mNGS and presence of fungal hyphae and spores in nasal mucosa

shortlist.label: Invasive fungal sinusitis
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of pansinusitis and presence of fungal hyphae and spores in nasal mucosa

shortlist.label: COVID-19-associated pulmonary aspergillosis
shortlist.why_kept: Recent COVID-19 infection and clinical presentation of bilateral lung infiltrations

shortlist.label: Diabetic ketoacidosis with fungal infection
shortlist.why_kept: Uncontrolled diabetes and presence of fungal hyphae and spores in nasal mucosa

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including nasal ache, dyspnea, and facial and nasal swelling, along with the presence of fungal hyphae and spores in the nasal mucosa and detection of Mucor racemosus in blood mNGS, are consistent with mucormycosis, a rare but serious fungal infection that often affects people with uncontrolled diabetes and immunocompromised individuals, especially after a COVID-19 infection.

rejected.label: Rhizopus infection
rejected.why: While Rhizopus microsporum was detected in blood mNGS, the overall clinical presentation and laboratory findings are more consistent with mucormycosis, which can be caused by various fungi including Rhizopus species.

rejected.label: Invasive fungal sinusitis
rejected.why: This diagnosis is too narrow, as the patient's condition involves not only sinusitis but also lung infiltrations and other systemic symptoms.

rejected.label: COVID-19-associated pulmonary aspergillosis
rejected.why: The patient's fungal infection is more consistent with mucormycosis, given the presence of fungal hyphae and spores in the nasal mucosa and the detection of Mucor racemosus, rather than aspergillosis.

rejected.label: Diabetic ketoacidosis with fungal infection
rejected.why: While the patient has uncontrolled diabetes, the primary issue is the fungal infection, which is more specifically identified as mucormycosis based on the clinical and laboratory findings.
